rationale:
Sixth and LAST handler config in this lane's real scope for bugs_open/334's commit_sha standardisation (RFC_029 step 5's real gate). Unlike the five already applied (519 page-rerender, 521 rerender-pages, 523 section-editor, 527 webdesign-agent, 528 nav-updater — all APPROVED, APPLIED, and confirmed live), page-build-handler has NO direct git_commit step of its own. It reaches one indirectly, one hop away, by calling page-rerender via its own deploy_page (call_agent, target_role: page_renderer, output_field: deploy_result). So this migration is only meaningful — and only correct — after migration 519 (page-rerender) shipped, which it did (APPROVED, applied 2026-08-21, verified end-to-end: a real completed page-rerender orchestration 19 seconds after the apply boundary showed deploy_result.response.data.commit_sha populated with a genuine sha, alongside rendered_page/deploy_result unchanged).

This migration's own guard makes that dependency explicit and checked, not assumed: it refuses to apply unless page-rerender's live config already exposes commit_sha via result_mapping. This is the FIRST migration in this batch with a real cross-agent dependency, and it is enforced in SQL, not just documented.
submitter: staged_component_build lane — RFC_029 §10.13 step 5's real gate (bdl/commit_sha), handler standardisation half, LAST of the batch

plan.summary: Convert page-build-handler's complete step from output_fields to result_mapping, preserving sections_saved and deploy_result byte-for-byte and adding commit_sha sourced from deploy_result.response.commit_sha (one level shallower than the other five migrations, since deploy_result here IS the call_agent envelope around page-rerender's own now-standardised response). Depends on and is guarded against migration 519, already approved and live.

edits.rationale: Converts page-build-handler's complete step from output_fields=["sections_saved","deploy_result"] to result_mapping with both as identity maps plus commit_sha sourced from deploy_result.response.commit_sha — ONE level shallower than the other five migrations in this batch, because page-build-handler's deploy_result IS the call_agent envelope wrapping page-rerender's OWN response, and 519 already put commit_sha at the top level of THAT response (alongside deploy_result/rendered_page, not nested inside them). Traced and measured, not assumed: a PRE-519 sample (orchestration cc6167b9, 2026-08-21 12:35Z) shows page-build-handler's deploy_result.response = {deploy_result: {...raw git result...}, rendered_page: {...}} — one .response hop down from its own deploy_result key, matching page-rerender's pre-519 output_fields shape exactly; post-519 the same shape gains one sibling key, commit_sha, at that same level. Guard additionally confirms deploy_page still targets page_renderer specifically (the assumption the whole mapped path rests on) and that page-rerender's own commit_sha mapping (519) is live before applying. Two page-build-handler paths bypass deploy_page entirely (mark_no_ready_sections/mark_writer_skipped, when there are no sections to write) and correctly show no deploy_result at all — [MEASURED] the two most recent completions took exactly this path; commit_sha correctly resolves absent there, unchanged by this file. complete_error (a separate step, output_fields=["page_content","site_record"]) never exposed deploy_result and is untouched.

Restores output_fields, refusing unless result_mapping is exactly what this migration wrote. Also notes that if migration 519 is ever rolled back, this file's mapped path silently stops resolving (absent field, not a crash) and should be rolled back too for cleanliness.

plan.risks:
1. THIS IS THE ONLY MIGRATION IN THE BATCH WITH A REAL CROSS-AGENT DEPENDENCY, and it is enforced in the guard (refuses if page-rerender's own commit_sha mapping is not live), not merely documented in prose.

2. NO POST-519 LIVE SAMPLE OF page-build-handler ACTUALLY CALLING page-rerender EXISTED AT WRITE TIME — page-build-handler's demand is intermittent and its last deploy_page call predates 519's apply by about an hour. The migration's own VERIFY block issues a WARNING (not an EXCEPTION) if this is still true at apply time, rather than blocking a migration whose correctness rests on 519 (independently verified) plus a traced, measured PRE-519 shape. The end-to-end proof will follow once page-build-handler completes a real deploy after this applies; noted honestly rather than claimed prematurely.

3. Same standing risk as the rest of the batch: no existing reader is assumed to depend on output_fields' MODE rather than the keys/values it produces.

4. This is the last of ~7 real handlers (6 direct/dependent + the two already-closed items in this lane, tg/reason and tg/related_pages, from earlier work). After this applies, the handler side of bugs_open/334 is COMPLETE, and the bdl-side wire becomes the bugfix_315/staged-component-build lane's, per the agreed split and ordering (config first, wire after).
